topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy for local tumor control
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how local treatments remove or destroy tumors and when accompanying chemotherapy can improve their effectiveness.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: action and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how broadly damaging cancer drugs achieve therapeutic effects while creating toxicity and opportunities for resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking hormone signaling restrains cancers that remain dependent on external growth signals.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing cell cycle checkpoint functions can make cancer cells selectively vulnerable to treatment.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting an additional DNA repair pathway selectively kills cancer cells already deficient in BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Oncogene-guided treatment and kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying cancer-driving oncogenes and inhibiting their activated protein products.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitor resistance and long-term treatment limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why cancer responses to kinase inhibitors can be undermined and how this shapes ongoing treatment.

topics.label: Antibody-directed targeting of cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognizing cell-surface proteins direct therapeutic effects toward cancer cells.

topics.label: Endogenous antitumor immunity and checkpoint blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether naturally occurring T-cell responses recognize cancer and how checkpoint blockade can strengthen those responses.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells toward cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered approaches that direct T-cell cytotoxicity toward selected tumor antigens.

topics.label: Matching treatment to heterogeneous cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why variable treatment responses require better patient selection while cancer plasticity continues to complicate therapy.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how prevention and earlier diagnosis contribute to observed improvements in cancer outcomes.

topics.label: Future cancer care and the ethics of advancing treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how further advances in cancer care must be weighed against the benefits and burdens of established treatments.
